title: Set-Asides Where a Chargeback Has Left an Account Short
content:
A part of the qualifying monthly earnings of a Keyturn Host Payout Account is set aside where the account itself has lately been left short by money a guest charged back.

**Where money charged back by a guest has been booked to the account in the three months up to that day and the netting of every entry on the account stands below nothing**, the short-account set-aside share of 5 percent applies.

**Where money charged back by a guest has been booked to the account in that period and the netting of every entry on the account stands at or above nothing**, the cleared-account set-aside share of 2 percent applies.

**In every other case**, nothing is set aside on that ground, the share standing at 0 percent.

The share is taken on the qualifying monthly earnings as first measured, and the sum set aside is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## The two tests, in order

The first test is whether money charged back by a guest has been booked to the account in the three months up to that day. Where none has, neither of the first two cases can be met and the third governs whatever the balance shows. Where such money has been booked in that period, the second test is the netting of every entry ever booked to the account: below nothing gives 5 percent, and at or above nothing gives 2 percent. A netting of exactly nothing stands at nothing rather than below it, so it falls in the second case.

## On hypothetical figures

Where the qualifying monthly earnings as first measured are 1200.00 USD, the sum set aside on this ground is 60.00 USD in the first case, 24.00 USD in the second and nothing at all in the third.
